title: Normalized scalar adjunction on K-flat models and the coefficient unit
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site with a final object [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology], let $n\geq1$, and put $Z=\mathbf Z_{\mathcal C}$ and $R=(\mathbf Z/n\mathbf Z)_{\mathcal C}$ [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf]. Use sheaves of modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] and their cohomological unbounded derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Put $E=-\otimes_Z R$ [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product], $Lq=-\otimes_Z^L R$ [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings], and let $\operatorname{Res}$ be restriction of scalars [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars]. Restriction is exact, and its right derived functor is termwise restriction. The ordinary adjunction $E\dashv\operatorname{Res}$ is specified by the inverse formulas $f\mapsto(a\mapsto f(a\otimes\bar1))$ and $g\mapsto(a\otimes r\mapsto r g(a))$. Let the derived adjunction be the one supplied by [new-derived-adjunction-compatibility] on K-flat resolving complexes [def-pc-kflat-complex]. Writing $\eta$ for its unit, for every K-flat complex $P$ the resolution comparison $c_P:Lq(P)\simeq E(P)$ satisfies
$$(\operatorname{Res}c_P)\eta_P=Q(P\longrightarrow\operatorname{Res}E(P)),\qquad x\longmapsto x\otimes\bar1,$$
where $Q$ denotes localization of complexes. With the shift structure on $Lq$ induced by this adjunction and exact restriction, $\eta$ commutes with every integer shift: $\eta_{X[k]}=\eta_X[k]$, with the canonical shift comparisons inserted.
The integer unit complex $Z[0]$ is K-flat, and there is a unique isomorphism $e:Lq(Z[0])\xrightarrow{\sim}R[0]$ whose adjunct is the actual coefficient quotient $q:Z[0]\to\operatorname{Res}R[0]$, that is
$$(\operatorname{Res}e)\eta_Z=q.$$
For any abelian sheaf $F$, residue-module sheaf $T$, quotient map $p:F\to\operatorname{Res}T$ with $p$ a cokernel of $n:F\to F$, and isomorphism $a:Lq(F[0])\simeq T[0]$ normalized by $(\operatorname{Res}a)\eta_F=p[0]$, every sheaf map $s:Z\to F$ has a unique residue-linear reduction $\bar s:R\to T$ satisfying $(\operatorname{Res}\bar s)q=ps$. Its map in the derived category satisfies
$$\bar s[0]=a\,Lq(s[0])\,e^{-1}.$$
All comparisons here use the natural single-complex/restriction identifications; no flatness of $R$ over $Z$ is assumed.
